about: The 65 -> 106 rig swap (Dom + Strategy 2026-10-26; docs/PLAN.md section 10). Every bone or weapon-node lookup in the fight goes through src/fight/rig-bones.ts, which only reads this file (Dom: everything on the data layer). `held`: the 65 rig's weapon-node names (the weapon always in hand or a grafted part, the drawn sword, the sheathed sword), the keys of `weapons`. `detect`: the joint that marks each rig. `bones`: a 65-joint name (V1's warrior/veteran skeleton, the name every lookup and data row uses) -> the 106-joint Mixamo name as the GLB spells it (three.js strips the ':' when it loads: mixamorig:Hips is the object mixamorigHips). `bones` is OpenTrident's map (src/assets/minotaur-106.bones.json `map`, test/rig-bones.test.mjs keeps them equal). `weapons`: a weapon-node name -> the names tried on a 106 body, first found wins: OpenTrident's fk_socket_hand_r first (it carries the 65 rig's WeaponDrawn/SwordDrawn frame; the file's old SwordDrawn node is ~12.7 degrees off), then the body's own node. `hide`: draws on a 106 body that are not shown (OpenTrident's armour layers: Dom 2026-10-26, no armour until after alpha/beta). `gapFill`: on a 106 body only, a role whose clip the body lacks plays the first of these clips it has (the dev bodies ch22/ch25 carry 12 clips; the real files carry the 65 rig's set and fill nothing). `grip65`: the 65 rig's sword hand an equip part hangs from (`hand`, unless the part names its own) and where the part's frame sits in it (warrior.glb's SwordDrawn: translation, rotation xyzw), so a part grafted on a 106 body lands where that body's own SwordDrawn (or fk_socket_hand_r) is. `files`: the 106 file stem under src/assets for a 65 body stem. `default`: which rig each side draws. 106 ONLY (Dom 2026-10-26: 'the opponent, which is the Minotaur, Pitborn, and also our own character ... will be moving forward, so there's no risk of going back to the old 65 rig'; docs/PLAN.md section 10): both '106', and no URL key picks a rig (the old ?rig= / ?foerig= are gone; test/rig-bones.test.mjs fails if a default is not '106' or a rig query key comes back). The 65 files stay only as the load's fallback when a 106 file fails.

clips106.about: The baked clip JSONs (src/assets/special-*.json, execution-*.json, hamstrung-*.json) are keyed to the 65 joints and posed wrong when bound by name on a 106 body (the joints' rest frames differ: the Skull Crack's sword arm swung out to the side). OpenTrident retargeted all eight to each 106 body (FK error <= 0.0006 deg, same key times and track order; the two sets differ only in pelvis.position, each fitted to its body). `dir`: a 106 body file stem (`files`' values) -> its folder under src/assets. `files`: a clip role -> its file name in that folder. A 106 body plays the file of ITS folder (the special's caster; the finisher's killer and victim each their own); a 65 body the 65 file under src/assets, as before. A role or body not listed here plays what it would without the clip (rig-bones.ts clip106Path; src/fight/clips-106.ts holds the lazy loaders, test/rig-bones.test.mjs keeps every path here loadable).

clipLoad.about: When a 106 body's baked clip JSONs are fetched (perf, 2026-10-26: on a slow link the hero's specials landed ~5 s after ready, so the first Skull Crack or Whirlwind of a visit played the weapon's plain swing). `hero`: the hero's own clip roles, fetched the moment its rig is built, ahead of anything else (scene.ts, once warriors are loaded; characters.ts prefetchClips; only a role its weapon plays, as on the first cast). `afterFirstFrame`: roles fetched on idle after the first frame, never before it (the Hamstrung finisher's killer and victim, the opponent's included). Everything else (the opponent's specials, the Execution) stays on first need. Which clip plays when is unchanged: this only moves when a file is requested.
